terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A source-faithful stylized world reconstruction with five action-ready landmark families; baked UI and approximate route geometry are excluded.

reasoning: The source combines a floating terrain system, dominant palace, four landmark families, distant colony, dense modular ornament, liquid/transparent materials and multiple independent ambience systems.
Action readiness requires separate named landmark roots, L1-L3 additive stages, focus sockets, occupancy envelopes, effect emitters and independently animated fauna/flow systems.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

resolvedImplementationDecisions: Occluded satellite and rear faces extend visible motif grammar at explicitly lower confidence.
The canonical Island Run camera, route, occupancy envelopes, and 36-tile topology override the source's baked UI and approximate path.
The source Arena card is adapted to a Nectar Trials Pavilion because Island 014 is an ordinary Mystery island, not an every-fifth Arena island.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At 390x844 the world reads immediately as the supplied bright Honeycomb Kingdom: fractured honey-rock island, blue cloud depth, honey falls, airborne bees and one dominant many-towered royal hive palace.
The five canonical landmarks have distinct footprint-stable silhouettes, named action-ready roots and explicit additive L1-L3 construction stories using the shared three-robot theatre.
Gold-bronze, wax-cream, amber/honey, dark rock, foliage and flower materials remain distinct under the shared camera without flattening into yellow plastic or excessive bloom.
Front, left, right and rear surveys preserve coherent façades and the real 36-tile route remains fully readable at phone scale.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Honeycomb civilization identity
qualityCriteria: Hex-cell architecture, honey channels, bees, flower terraces and distant hive islets form one working civilization rather than disconnected gold props.
Blue sky and cream cloud depth remain a strong cool counterfield behind the warm city.
failureModes: generic yellow fantasy castle
gold city loses bees, honey or flower ecology
background collapses to flat blue

featureGroups.name: Royal hive palace dominance
qualityCriteria: The broad stair, central portal, amber dome, stacked drum, side towers and royal bee/purple accents produce the source's dominant central silhouette.
Satellite landmarks remain subordinate and do not repeat the palace tower stack.
failureModes: palace reads as one generic dome
satellites repeat palace silhouette
central mass is too small at phone scale

featureGroups.name: Construction and commissioning readiness
qualityCriteria: Every landmark exposes retained/additive parts for five semantic reveal stages and compact honey-language façade staging.
The three robots remain outside occupancy envelopes and newly commissioned parts use the shared bounded pop, flash and sparkle finish.
failureModes: whole-model fade
missing robot role
funded geometry scales
unsafe strobing or looping particles

featureGroups.name: Phone composition and runtime budget
qualityCriteria: The whole route and all five landmarks fit between the live HUD and controller at 390x844.
Repeated cells, flowers, bees and distant islets use batching, instancing or quality-scaled counts.
failureModes: route or landmark hidden by scenery
micro-detail dominates draw calls
quality tiers change labels but not cost

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

featureReviews.notes: The render is a compact blob cluster instead of a tiered floating island.
No readable central palace tower stack or royal dome.
Cells, honey falls, flowers, and bees are absent from the macro render.
The four satellites read as unrelated primitive shapes.

visualEvidence.notes: Tier 1 also failed silhouette IoU at 0.243 and scale delta at 0.746; multi-angle review detected a degenerate orbit view.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The palette correction is visible, but structure is the dominant failure. The source is vertically tiered and palace-led; the render is horizontally clustered and primitive-led. Refining materials cannot rescue this silhouette.

featureReviews.notes: Central stacked palace reads clearly but is much less ornate than the source.
Gold, cells, bees, islets and honey falls read, but garden and facade density remain low.
Five families are structurally distinct in the live world and construction routes, though small at overview scale.
Main crown, satellites, undersides, falls and distant islets hold in overview and orbit views.
The first integrated capture has isolated flowers rather than the source's lush planted terraces.

visualEvidence.notes: User explicitly accepted this as the correct production direction. Acceptance of direction is not treated as a 0.7 fidelity pass.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Tier 1 passes because the full-frame UI-like images share framing and background; this does not prove visual fidelity. Direct vision comparison places the integrated pass around 0.58. The procedural world is correctly identified, but the source is much denser, brighter, greener and more ornate. The required next action is refine-code, not continue.

featureReviews.notes: The bright stacked palace remains the unmistakable central hierarchy at phone scale.
Cream/amber/gold route, bees, honey drops and planted cells strengthen the identity, but the source has substantially denser lattice architecture.
All five families and their live construction routes are distinct, though the overview crops the rear satellites tightly.
Main crown, satellites, pointed undersides and wider honey drops retain clear actual-3D depth.
Green beds and more flowers improve the terraces, but they remain much sparser than the lush goal image.

visualEvidence.notes: Eivind accepted the actual-3D direction before this refinement. Remaining fidelity and device performance are preserved as explicit follow-up gates.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Direct comparison confirms a large improvement over the rejected blockout and a smaller but visible refinement over the first integrated capture. It does not meet the 0.7 visual-release threshold because micro-architecture and planted density remain lower than the goal. Stop means the requested implementation slice is complete and honestly gated, not that physical release or pixel-level fidelity passed.

featureReviews.notes: User-accepted drift; generic radial front remains explicit.
Closed deep side/rear volume is stable.
Next authorized facade slice must create the inhabited cathedral identity.

visualEvidence.notes: User-accepted drift applies only to the palace macro. Other part and final island gates remain unchanged.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: This is not a visual pass or a threshold reduction. It records the user's explicit authority to continue dependent work with the known 0.60 palace macro drift.

featureReviews.notes: The vertically stretched jewel-hive cathedral now owns the phone silhouette.
Honey cells, satellites, bees and amber architecture read, but source density is higher.
All five families remain distinct across front, side and rear orbit evidence.
Main crown, satellites, undersides and distant islets remain volumetric from six angles.
The runtime contains dense batched gardens, but the offline source-return still reads sparser than the goal.
Geometry and physical-material parameters are present; CPU projection cannot prove refraction and glistening.
Amber ripples and crown now frame the palace, but live GPU phone verification remains required.

visualEvidence.notes: CPU triangle projection uses actual meshes and instance transforms but approximates physical materials and omits live route tiles/post-processing.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Direct vision review of the source-return sheet places the whole pass at 0.71. The macro island and palace hierarchy are substantially closer than the prior 0.64 capture. This does not meet release: illustrated garden density, small hive richness and the delicious translucent honey response are not all proven at or above 0.75. Tier 1 passed on 320-pixel immutable derivatives (IoU 0.9464) but warned both frames were not isolated, so it is structural evidence only.

featureReviews.notes: The tall jewel-hive cathedral remains the dominant phone-scale silhouette.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto: Warm key light from upper camera-left, soft-edged and strong enough to separate palace bevels without clipping amber highlights.
Cool blue fill from the sky and cream cloud field preserves shadow detail in dark rock fractures.
Warm rim/environment reflection from camera-right catches gold edges, bee wings, and honey curtains.
Use ACES filmic tone mapping with restrained exposure and bloom so purple enamel and blue sky remain saturated.
Contact shadows and ambient occlusion ground every landmark, terrace overlap, stair, and robot construction placement.
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
